title_en: Hong Xiufeng v. Kunming Anbeijia Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. — dispute over house sales contract
ruling_gist_en: 1. A contract is, by nature, original evidence and direct evidence. Its higher probative value compared to hearsay evidence and circumstantial evidence should be recognized, and it should serve as the logical starting point and fundamental basis for determining the nature of the legal relationship between the parties. To deny the legal relationship reflected in written evidence and to determine the existence of other civil legal relationships between the parties that are not documented in written evidence, a more cautious analysis and evaluation must be conducted in the examination of evidence.

full_text_en:
Hong Xiufeng v. Kunming Anbeijia Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. — Dispute over Contract for Sale of Commercial Housing

Ruling Summary

1. A contract is, in nature, original evidence and direct evidence, and due weight should be given to its relatively high probative value as compared with derivative evidence and circumstantial evidence, and it should serve as the logical starting point and basic basis for determining the nature of the legal relationship between the parties. To deny the legal relationship reflected in written evidence and to determine the existence of other civil legal relationships between the parties that lack written evidence as a carrier, a more cautious analysis and determination must be made in the review of evidence.

2. In situations where two interpretations are equally reasonable, the determination should be made in favor of the establishment of the legal relationship represented by the written evidence, thereby conveying and establishing the value orientation of honoring promises and upholding good faith.

3. In determining the nature of the disputed legal relationship through interpretation, the basic value orientation should be to clarify, rather than obscure, the rights and obligations under the disputed legal relationship. In the absence of sufficient evidence to prove the existence of a hidden legal relationship between the parties and that such hidden legal relationship is genuine and ultimately binding on the parties, it is inappropriate to simply deny the reflection and manifestation of the parties' true intentions by the existing externalized legal relationship, so as to avoid the result that one party improperly escapes from the established rights and obligations.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2015) Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 78

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Hong Xiufeng, female, Han ethnicity, born July 25, 1990, residing in Nan'an City, Fujian Province.

Agent ad litem: Wan Qiuqin, attorney at Beijing Zhong Lun Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Shen Hanqing, attorney at Yunnan Baqian Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Kunming Anbeijia Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 32 Wujing Road, Kunming City, Yunnan Province.

Legal Representative: Zhang Xiaoxia, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Yang Xiaoping, attorney at Yunnan Ruixin Law Firm.

In the case concerning the dispute over a contract for the sale of commercial housing between Appellant Hong Xiufeng and Respondent Kunming Anbeijia Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Anbeijia Company), the Yunnan High People's Court rendered the Civil Judgment (2014) Yun Gao Min Yi Chu Zi No. 9 on December 17, 2014. Hong Xiufeng, dissatisfied with the judgment, appealed to this Court. Upon acceptance, this Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a public hearing on April 23, 2015. Wan Qiuqin and Shen Hanqing, the agents ad litem of Hong Xiufeng, and Yang Xiaoping, the agent ad litem of Anbeijia Company, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. The case is now concluded.

The court of first instance found the following facts: On August 21, 2013, Anbeijia Company (Party A) and Hong Xiufeng (Party B) signed two "Contracts for the Purchase and Sale of Commercial Housing," specifying the details of Hong Xiufeng's purchase of the first and second floor commercial units of the Baifuqi Commercial Plaza developed by Anbeijia Company. Contract No. 001 stipulated: The first-floor commercial premises were priced by the usable floor area, with a usable area of 3,143.02 square meters, a unit price of RMB 20,000 per square meter (including the price of the apportioned common area), and a total amount of RMB 62,860,400; Party B was to pay RMB 56,574,360 before August 18, 2013, and RMB 6,286,040 before January 20, 2014; the delivery time was December 14, 2013; if Party A delayed delivery, it would pay Party B liquidated damages of RMB 314,302 per day for the period from the day after the delivery deadline to the actual date of delivery, up to 30 days, with the contract to continue to be performed. If the delay exceeded 30 days, Party A would pay liquidated damages of 0.5% of the total purchase price, and the contract would continue. Contract No. 002 stipulated: The second-floor commercial premises were priced by the usable floor area, with a usable area of 3,601.29 square meters, a unit price of RMB 9,869 per square meter (including the price of the apportioned common area), and a total amount of RMB 35,541,130; Party B was to pay RMB 31,987,017 before August 18, 2013, and RMB 3,554,113 before January 20, 2014; the delivery time and liability for breach were the same as those in Contract No. 001. On the same day, the parties filed the two contracts for registration and record. Hong Xiufeng, in accordance with the payment instructions in the payment authorization letter issued by Anbeijia Company, transferred RMB 56,574,360 and RMB 22,825,640 by bank transfer on the same day to the account designated in the letter, and also remitted RMB 19,000,000 to Zhang Xiaoxia, the legal representative of Anbeijia Company, totaling RMB 98,400,000. Anbeijia Company issued ten receipts to Hong Xiufeng, each for RMB 9,840,000, totaling RMB 98,400,000. On August 26, 2013, and September 18, 2013, Zhang Xiaoxia remitted RMB 3,680,000 each time to Hong Xiufeng.

The court of first instance also found: On October 28, 2011, the Baifuqi Commercial Plaza was completed and accepted for use. On June 2, 2013, Anbeijia Company entered into a "Shop Lease Contract" with Kunming Libang House Demolition Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Libang Company), leasing the first and second floor commercial units of the Baifuqi Commercial Plaza to Libang Company for a period from June 1, 2013, to May 31, 2033.

Hong Xiufeng filed a lawsuit, alleging: After the parties signed the two "Contracts for the Purchase and Sale of Commercial Housing" on August 21, 2013, Hong Xiufeng paid the full purchase price in accordance with the contract, but Anbeijia Company refused to perform its contractual obligations. Therefore, the claims were: 1. To order Anbeijia Company to deliver the entire first and second floor commercial units of Building A of Kunming Baifuqi Commercial Plaza, and to assist Hong Xiufeng in obtaining the ownership certificate within 40 days after delivery; 2. To order Anbeijia Company to bear the liability for late delivery and pay liquidated damages of RMB 19,350,128; 3. The case acceptance fee, attorney's fees (RMB 3,000,000), and other related expenses to be borne by Anbeijia Company.

Anbeijia Company defended, arguing: The case was in substance a private lending dispute, and the commercial housing sale contract was merely a form of guarantee for the private loan and should be invalid. Hong Xiufeng's claim for liquidated damages for late delivery had no contractual or legal basis. The case acceptance fee should be determined by the court, and attorney's fees were not necessarily incurred.

The court of first instance, after trial, held that: (1) Although the parties formally signed the "Contracts for the Purchase and Sale of Commercial Housing," the Baifuqi Commercial Plaza had been completed and accepted for use on October 28, 2011, and the property in question was leased in its entirety to Libang Company before the parties signed the contract, and Hong Xiufeng was aware of this. In a situation where delivery conditions were already met, the parties agreed to a delivery date of December 14, 2013, which was contrary to common sense. (2) From the "Contract for the Purchase and Sale of Commercial Housing" between Anbeijia Company and an unrelated party, Zhang Linjie, dated April 9, 2010, the agreed price for the fourth-floor commercial units of the Baifuqi Commercial Plaza was RMB 40,936.06 per square meter, while the transaction prices for the first and second floors in this case were RMB 20,000 per square meter and RMB 9,869 per square meter, significantly lower than the price agreed between Anbeijia Company and the unrelated party. (3) Hong Xiufeng should have paid the full purchase price in two installments by January 20, 2014, but on the day of signing, she remitted RMB 56,574,360 and RMB 22,825,640 to Anbeijia Company, and also remitted RMB 19,000,000 to Anbeijia Company's legal representative Zhang Xiaoxia (totaling RMB 98,400,000), paying the full purchase price immediately, which was inconsistent with the payment habits of a normal home buyer. After receiving the above payments, Anbeijia Company issued ten receipts instead of purchase invoices to Hong Xiufeng, which also violated trade customs in real estate sales. (4) In the absence of any other business dealings between Hong Xiufeng and Anbeijia Company, Zhang Xiaoxia, the legal representative of Anbeijia Company, remitted RMB 3,680,000 each to Hong Xiufeng on August 26, 2013, and September 18, 2013. Regarding this amount, Anbeijia Company argued that the actual loan amount between it and Hong Xiufeng was RMB 80,000,000, with a monthly interest rate of 4.6%, and the monthly interest was RMB 3,680,000. Hong Xiufeng argued that the RMB 7,360,000 was a sales rebate from Anbeijia Company to her, but this was not stipulated in the contract, nor was there any other evidence to substantiate it. The above series of actions by the parties clearly did not conform to general trade customs in real estate sales, so it should be determined that the "Contracts for the Purchase and Sale of Commercial Housing" were in name a real estate sale but in substance a loan guarantee, and the legal relationship between the parties was a civil legal relationship of loan, in name a real estate sale. Hong Xiufeng's claim that the legal relationship between her and Anbeijia Company was a real estate sale was inconsistent with the legal relationship found by the court. The court of first instance clarified this to Hong Xiufeng, but she insisted on her claims without amendment. In summary, the court of first instance, in accordance with Article 152 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Articles 2 and 35 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Procedures, rendered a judgment dismissing Hong Xiufeng's claims. The case acceptance fee of RMB 630,558.30 was borne by Hong Xiufeng.

Hong Xiufeng, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to this Court.

Hong Xiufeng appealed, arguing: The court of first instance erred in fact-finding and application of law by characterizing a very clear contract for sale as a loan relationship in the guise of a real estate sale. The four grounds relied upon by the first-instance judgment had no factual or legal basis. Therefore, she requested that the first-instance judgment be reversed and all her claims be upheld.

Anbeijia Company defended, arguing: The first-instance court's finding that the legal relationship in this case was a loan in the guise of a real estate sale was objective and truthful, and the dismissal of Hong Xiufeng's claims was based on clear factual findings. Therefore, it requested that the appeal be dismissed and the first-instance judgment be upheld.

This Court found the following additional facts in the second instance: On August 14, 2013, Anbeijia Company issued a payment authorization letter authorizing Hong Xiufeng to remit the purchase price of RMB 98,400,000 to accounts of Zhang Xiaoxia and the company. A bank card withdrawal business receipt from the Wujing Road Sub-branch of Agricultural Bank of China Limited, Kunming, recorded that Zhang Xiaoxia transferred RMB 18,400,000 into the account of Wu Jixie on August 21, 2013. On August 21, 2013, Anbeijia Company issued ten receipts, stating that it had received a total of RMB 98,400,000 in purchase payments from Hong Xiufeng. On August 26, 2013, and September 18, 2013, Zhang Xiaoxia remitted RMB 3,680,000 each to Hong Xiufeng, and the purpose of the remittances was recorded as "private remittance."

At the first-instance trial on September 23, 2014, Anbeijia Company stated that the Baifuqi Commercial Plaza had four floors of commercial units, some of which were leased out and some were sold, and the unit price for sales was RMB 18,000 per square meter. At the second-instance trial, Anbeijia Company stated that the price for the fourth-floor commercial units of the Baifuqi Commercial Plaza was RMB 18,000 per square meter at the time of initial listing. This Court inquired of Anbeijia Company: "What was the reason for Zhang Xiaoxia's payment of RMB 18,400,000 to Wu Jixie? Was it based on Hong Xiufeng's instructions? Is there any evidence?" and "Who is Wu Jixie?" Anbeijia Company replied that the payment was a refund to Wu Jixie, and there was no evidence that the remittance was based on Hong Xiufeng's instructions; Zhang Xiaoxia knew Wu Jixie before the loan and did not know Hong Xiufeng; Wu Jixie was the general manager of Lianheng Investment, Hong Jianhua was the chairman of Lianheng Investment, and Hong Xiufeng and Hong Jianhua were relatives. This Court inquired of Hong Xiufeng about the relationship between her and Hong Jianhua, and she replied that it needed verification.

Hong Xiufeng submitted eleven "second-instance new evidence" items in court, namely: 1. Photographs taken by Hong Xiufeng during her on-site inspection of the property in question, proof purpose: Before signing the contract, Hong Xiufeng conducted an on-site inspection, and her true intention was to purchase the property; 2. Various development and construction documents and permits provided by Anbeijia Company to Hong Xiufeng, proof purpose: Hong Xiufeng paid close attention to the legality of the property; 3. The mobile phone call log of Hong Xiufeng's first-instance attorney Shen Hanqing for November 2014, a CD and transcript of a phone call between Shen Hanqing and Anbeijia Company's legal representative Zhang Xiaoxia on November 10, 2014 (time: 12:12, duration: 4 minutes 54 seconds), the main content of which was discussing the resale of the property to the lessee. In the call, Zhang Xiaoxia said: "Because we have changed the property owner, his idea is whether he could buy it, and I told him, he had previously proposed to buy it, so I told you to hurry up and prepare to sell it to him." Proof purpose: After the first-instance trial, Zhang Xiaoxia admitted that Hong Xiufeng was the property owner of the property and had the right to decide to resell the property to others or collect rent from the lessee; 4. The "Lease Contract for Business Premises" between Kunming Aojia Property Services Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Aojia Company) and Ping An Bank Co., Ltd., Kunming Branch, signed on May 13, 2013, provided by Anbeijia Company to Hong Xiufeng, proof purpose: During the negotiation of the real estate sale, Anbeijia Company provided this lease contract to demonstrate the investment value of the property; 5. News reports about the suspected illegal construction of Baifuqi Commercial Plaza, proof purpose: Because Hong Xiufeng learned of this issue before purchasing, the parties made realistic agreements on the transaction price and delivery date; 6. The certificate of permission to move the household registration of Zhang Xiaoxia and Zhang Chuanwen, the stub of the household registration transfer certificate, and a printed web page of Zhang Chuanwen's citizen ID number query, showing that Zhang Chuanwen (female, ID number 5302×××××××××××, upgraded to 5302××××××××××××××) moved her household registration from "Dongchuan City Tangdan Town 314 Team" to "Southwest Nonferrous Geology Bureau 309 Team" on March 20, 1998, with the reason being "family accompanying relocation." Proof purpose: Zhang Linjie and Zhang Chuanwen are the same person, and she has a family relationship with Anbeijia Company's legal representative Zhang Xiaoxia, casting doubt on the authenticity of the "Contract for the Purchase and Sale of Commercial Housing" between them; 7. The registration record of the revocation of the "Contract for the Purchase and Sale of Commercial Housing" between Zhang Linjie and Anbeijia Company (contract registration number: KM2010042018568), proof purpose: (1) The total price of the unit purchased by Zhang Linjie was RMB 8,427,250, which translates to only RMB 5,000 per square meter, not the RMB 40,936.06 per square meter determined by the first-instance judgment. (2) The "Contract for the Purchase and Sale of Commercial Housing" was revoked on April 22, 2014 (before the first-instance trial) (type of revocation: revocation due to cancellation), and Anbeijia Company deliberately concealed the facts, misleading the first-instance court into rendering an erroneous judgment; 8-9. Transcripts of the first-instance court's trials on September 23, 2014, and October 23, 2014. According to the records, Anbeijia Company made inconsistent statements regarding the nature of the RMB 18,400,000 payment to Wu Jixie as "principal" and "interest," and also gave contradictory statements on the loan term, interest calculation standard, and interest payment timing. Proof purpose: Anbeijia Company could not give a consistent account of the alleged loan relationship; 10. Notice of the General Office of Kunming Municipal People's Government on Forwarding the Implementation Opinions on Further Strengthening the Management of Pre-sale of Commercial Housing in Kunming, Article 2, Paragraph 1 of which states: "For commercial housing projects that have obtained pre-sale permits, real estate development enterprises shall, within 10 days, publicly disclose to the public all approved units for sale and the price of each unit, as verified by the administrative department of housing and urban-rural development, and strictly sell in accordance with the declared price and clear pricing. If the actual selling price deviates by more than 15% from the declared price, it must be re-declared in a timely manner, with a limit of one re-declaration; otherwise, the real estate registration authority will not register for the record." Proof purpose: The contract in question was filed with the real estate management department, and the agreed price was within the price range declared by Anbeijia Company to the real estate management department; 11. The "Shop Lease Contract" between Anbeijia Company and Libang Company dated June 2, 2013, the authorization letter from Libang Company dated June 10, 2013, authorizing Aojia Company to lease the Baifuqi Commercial Plaza, and registration cards of the three companies, proof purpose: There is a related relationship between Anbeijia Company and Aojia Company, the rent price agreed between Anbeijia Company and Libang Company is only one percent of that of the actual lessee, and the signing date of the contract between Aojia Company and the actual lessee is earlier than the "Shop Lease Contract," making the transaction price and timing of this contract illogical.

The above evidence items 8-9 are transcripts of the first-instance court's trials and are not new evidence in the second-instance proceedings. The other evidence also existed during the first-instance proceedings, but considering the overall circumstances of the case, Hong Xiufeng's late submission of such evidence can hardly be considered intentional or grossly negligent. Based on the relevance of the evidence to the basic facts of the case, this Court ordered Anbeijia Company to submit its opinions on the authentication of the aforementioned evidence items 3, 6, 7, and 10 within a specified period.

At the second-instance trial, Anbeijia Company argued that none of the above evidence constituted new evidence. Regarding the relevant evidence, Anbeijia Company submitted its authentication opinions after the second-instance trial: 1. The phone call between Shen Hanqing and Zhang Xiaoxia occurred during the mediation process between the parties at the request of the first-instance judge on how to repay the loan, and its content does not prove that Hong Xiufeng is the property owner; 2. The ID numbers of Zhang Linjie and Zhang Chuanwen are the same, but it is unknown whether they are related to Zhang Xiaoxia; 3. Regarding Zhang Linjie's contract registration record and the price of the unit, Anbeijia Company provided the notarized purchase contract, personal housing mortgage loan contract, invoice for the initial payment of RMB 37,418,000, and the "Preliminary Result of Real Estate Appraisal Report" issued by Beijing Zhongqi Hua Real Estate Appraisal Co., Ltd. on October 10, 2014 (conclusion: the preliminary market value of the property with a total construction area of 19,794.54 square meters, including the first to fourth floor commercial units, all fourth-floor apartments, and basement parking spaces of Baifuqi Commercial Plaza, was RMB 702,000,000 as of September 24, 2014), arguing that the registered price in the contract was significantly lower than the market price at that time; 4. The Implementation Opinions on Further Strengthening the Management of Pre-sale of Commercial Housing in Kunming are genuine, but they came into effect on January 1, 2011, and the sales time of the project in question was January 3, 2010, when there was no requirement to publicly announce and declare prices.

Considering Anbeijia Company's authentication opinions, since it did not raise any objection to the authenticity of Hong Xiufeng's second-instance evidence items 3, 6, 7, and 10, this Court confirms their authenticity.

At the first-instance trial on September 23, 2014, Anbeijia Company stated that the property in question should have been completed and accepted for use, but the property ownership certificate had not yet been obtained due to planning issues, specifically because the planned number of floors was 25, but later 32 floors were built, and the additional floors were supposed to be approved in two batches, but they were built before the approval. In the agency opinion submitted by Hong Xiufeng after the second-instance trial, she did not explain the relationship between her and Hong Jianhua, and stated that the reason why the property ownership certificate for Baifuqi Commercial Plaza could not be obtained was suspected illegal construction beyond the approved limits, and that Anbeijia Company could obtain the property ownership registration after paying the fine in accordance with the law.

Other facts found by this Court are the same as those found by the court of first instance.

Opinion of the Court

Pursuant to the parties' submissions on appeal and in response, as confirmed by them in court, the issues in dispute on appeal are as follows: 1. the nature of the legal relationship between the parties; 2. whether Anbeijia Company should deliver the property in question to Hong Xiufeng and assist in completing the registration of change of ownership; 3. whether and how Anbeijia Company should bear liability for breach of contract for delayed delivery, and whether it should bear the attorney's fees paid by Hong Xiufeng.

I. The nature of the legal relationship between the parties

A civil legal relationship is a relationship of civil rights and obligations between civil subjects formed in the process of social relations being regulated by civil legal norms. Except as otherwise specifically provided by law, the creation, modification, or termination of a civil legal relationship requires a consensus of the intentions of the participants in the legal relationship. Ascertaining the consensus of intentions formed when civil subjects establish a specific legal relationship in accordance with legal norms aims to clarify the boundaries and content of the parties' rights and obligations. The conclusion of a civil transaction, particularly one as significant as the present case, often involves a complex background and is not accomplished overnight or set in stone. It is not uncommon for the parties' expression of intent to undergo certain changes and ultimately become clear during this process. Some transactions already established through contracts may have precisely experienced a process in which the parties transformed the nature of the legal relationship. However, due to considerations of their respective litigation interests, not all details during the formation of the transaction can be supported by valid litigation evidence. A contract, by its nature, is primary and direct evidence. According to Article 77 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Proceedings regarding the principle for determining the probative force of evidence, it should serve as the logical starting point and basic basis for determining the nature of the legal relationship between the parties, and its higher probative force relative to derivative evidence and circumstantial evidence should be respected. Only when there is sufficient evidence to prove that the actual performance of the parties significantly differs from the expressed intent of the effect manifested by the written contract documents can the nature of the legal relationship be determined based on the former. That is, except in circumstances where further verification of relevant facts beyond the written evidence is necessary due to specific legal policy considerations, overturning the probative force of written evidence should be the exception. The case facts in civil litigation should be those that can be proven by valid evidence. Furthermore, in determining the nature of a disputed legal relationship through interpretation, the basic value orientation should be to make the rights and obligations under the disputed legal relationship clearer, rather than more ambiguous. In the absence of sufficient evidence to support the existence of a hidden legal relationship between the parties and that such hidden legal relationship is genuine and ultimately binding on the parties, it is inappropriate to simply deny that the existing externalized legal relationship reflects the true intent of the parties, so as to avoid the result that a party improperly escapes the established rights and obligations. Moreover, even in cases where two interpretations are equally reasonable, the determination should be made in favor of the establishment of the legal relationship represented by the written evidence, thereby conveying and establishing the value orientation of honoring commitments and keeping promises. In summary, to deny the legal relationship reflected by the written evidence and determine the existence of another civil legal relationship between the parties not embodied in written evidence, a more prudent analysis and judgment in the review of evidence is required.

According to Article 7 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation (II) on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, a "trade usage" refers to a practice that does not violate the mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations, which is commonly adopted in the locality or in a specific field or industry of the transaction and is known or should be known by the counterparty at the time of contracting, or a habitual practice frequently used by the parties. The relevant provisions of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China regarding "trade usages" are intended to improve and supplement the content of the parties' rights and obligations and to enhance the certainty of the parties' contractual rights and obligations. The present case does not involve the use of trade usages to remedy the lack of certainty of rights and obligations caused by unclear or incomplete contractual terms. Beyond the aforementioned legislative intent, the use of "trade usages" to determine the "suspiciousness" of the parties' transaction conduct should be approached with extreme caution.

First, regarding the time of delivery of the property. The property in question was constructed with illegal excess floors beyond the planned permit and was sold without prior approval. In such circumstances, the parties agreed to deliver the property nearly four months after the signing of the contract. Even disregarding the above facts, in the case of a sale of existing property, it is highly questionable how the delivery period should be agreed upon to conform to "trade usages," whether it is necessary or has even formed a "trade usage," and whether a general consensus on similar ordinary transaction judgments has been reached.

Second, regarding the price of the property. Setting aside whether this relates to "trade usages," the determination of an unreasonably low price must also be based on the price information of equivalent properties published by the local real estate management authorities at the time. Although Anbeijia Company stated that it did not know whether Zhang Xiaoxia, its legal representative, and Zhang Linjie were relatives, it confirmed that Zhang Linjie and Zhang Chuanwen (who had the same residence registration migration time, reason, place of origin, and place of destination as Zhang Xiaoxia) had the same ID number. The filing record of the Commercial Housing Purchase and Sale Contract between Zhang Linjie and Anbeijia Company had been canceled due to the return of the property on April 22, 2014 (the first instance trial was held on September 23, 2014). The court of first instance did not ascertain the relevant facts, nor did it pay necessary attention to the fact that Anbeijia Company's statements made during the first instance trial significantly differed from the unit price stipulated in the aforementioned contract. It directly denied the existence of a commercial housing sale legal relationship between the parties in this case on the main ground that the price agreed by the parties was significantly lower than the price stipulated in the contract between Anbeijia Company and Zhang Linjie nearly 30 months before the date of the contract in this case. This reasoning lacks basis. Furthermore, at the time the parties in this case signed the contract (August 21, 2013), the implementation opinions of Kunming Municipality on further strengthening the management of pre-sale of commercial housing had already been implemented locally (effective January 1, 2011). According to the relevant provisions of these opinions, it can be determined that Hong Xiufeng's assertion that the transaction price in this case was within a reasonable range is valid.

Third, regarding the payment issue. The payment method for the purchase price under the contract in question was installment payment. However, given that Hong Xiufeng made a lump sum payment and Anbeijia Company accepted it, this should be considered a modification of the contract performance. Regarding this modification of contract performance as contrary to the payment habits of normal homebuyers lacks sufficient basis. Moreover, Hong Xiufeng's payment of RMB 19,000,000 to Zhang Xiaoxia, the legal representative of Anbeijia Company, also complied with the requirements of the payment authorization letter issued by the company. The purchase invoice is necessary for the parties to complete the real estate registration of change. The court of first instance held that Anbeijia Company's prior issuance of a receipt for the purchase price violated the "trade usage" of commercial housing sales and concluded that there was no commercial housing sale legal relationship between the parties, which lacks sufficient factual and legal basis. As for the nature of the RMB 7,360,000 payment, both parties' statements lack a contractual basis and are unsupported by other evidence. However, as discussed above, it is also inappropriate to overturn the conclusion that the legal relationship reflected by the written evidence exists between the parties through interpretation and inference based on this point.

Finally, regarding the issue of a loan legal relationship. Hong Xiufeng and Anbeijia Company signed a commercial housing purchase and sale contract and had it registered. During actual performance, although certain facts may give rise to different understandings and judgments, in the absence of any direct evidence of a private lending legal relationship between Hong Xiufeng and Anbeijia Company, and given that Anbeijia Company's statements on many core elements of the private lending legal relationship it asserts are inconsistent, finding a private lending legal relationship between the parties lacks sufficient factual basis. During the second instance trial of this case, a recording of a telephone conversation between Shen Hanqing and Zhang Xiaoxia, the legal representative of Anbeijia Company, on November 10, 2014 (after the first instance trial) was played in court. At that time, Anbeijia Company's defense position in the first instance had already been established, but Zhang Xiaoxia, the legal representative of Anbeijia Company, acknowledged Hong Xiufeng's status as a property buyer in the conversation. As for Anbeijia Company's claim that the RMB 18,400,000 paid to Wu Jixie was principal of a loan it had repaid, this court finds it difficult to accept due to the lack of any supporting evidence. If there is a dispute, the parties may seek resolution through other legal channels.

The standard of proof is the degree of proof that the person bearing the burden of proof must achieve in providing evidence to prove the legal facts they assert. In this case, Hong Xiufeng has completed the burden of proof for the existence of a commercial housing sale legal relationship between the parties, while Anbeijia Company asserts the existence of a private lending legal relationship between itself and Hong Xiufeng. According to Article 108 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, Anbeijia Company's evidence must be sufficient in probative force to make the people's court highly probable that the fact to be proven exists. Based on the foregoing, the evidence adduced by Anbeijia Company to rebut the facts asserted by Hong Xiufeng has not reached the standard of proof of high probability. Compared to the general standard of proof of high probability, the exclusion of reasonable doubt is a special standard of proof. Article 109 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China clearly stipulates the scope of special types of civil cases to which the principle of exclusion of reasonable doubt applies. The court of first instance found that a series of behaviors by the parties were manifestly inconsistent with the "trade usages" of commercial housing sales, and then concluded, based on reasonable doubt, that the legal relationship between them was a private lending legal relationship in the name of a housing sale. This conclusion lacks sufficient factual and legal basis and does not conform to the spirit of the aforementioned judicial interpretation. This court corrects this.

II. Whether Anbeijia Company should deliver the property in question to Hong Xiufeng and assist in completing the registration of change of ownership

The two Commercial Housing Purchase and Sale Contracts signed between Anbeijia Company and Hong Xiufeng do not violate the mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations regarding validity and should be deemed valid. Articles 8 and 60(1) of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provide that a lawfully formed contract is protected by law, and the parties shall fully perform their obligations in accordance with the agreement. Since Hong Xiufeng has paid the full purchase price in accordance with the contract, Anbeijia Company shall, in accordance with the law and the contract, deliver the property to Hong Xiufeng and assist in completing the registration of change of ownership. The fact that Baifuqi Commercial Plaza has illegal excess construction pertains to administrative violations, not specifically to the disputed property in this case. There are no legal or factual obstacles to Anbeijia Company's delivery of the property to Hong Xiufeng. This court supports Hong Xiufeng's claim for Anbeijia Company to deliver the property in question. However, since the aforementioned administrative violations constitute a legal obstacle to the registration of change of ownership of the property in question, it is not appropriate to directly order Anbeijia Company to perform the obligation of completing the registration of change of ownership in this judgment. Anbeijia Company shall assist Hong Xiufeng in completing the registration of change of ownership after the relevant administrative violations are resolved. If further disputes arise due to new facts regarding subsequent matters, Hong Xiufeng may seek resolution through other legal channels.

III. Whether and how Anbeijia Company should bear liability for breach of contract for delayed delivery, and whether it should bear the attorney's fees paid by Hong Xiufeng

Article 107 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides that if a party fails to perform its contractual obligations, or performs them in a manner that does not conform to the agreement, it shall bear liability for breach, such as continuing performance, taking remedial measures, or compensating for losses. In this case, Anbeijia Company's delay in delivery constitutes a breach of contract and shall bear corresponding liability in accordance with the law. According to the parties' agreement on liability for breach of contract for delayed delivery by Anbeijia Company, the liquidated damages payable by Anbeijia Company are as follows: RMB 314,302 x 30 days x 2 = RMB 18,858,120; RMB 62,860,400 x 5‰ = RMB 314,302; RMB 35,541,130 x 5‰ = RMB 177,705.65; totaling RMB 19,350,127.65. Hong Xiufeng's claim that Anbeijia Company should bear liability for breach in the amount of RMB 19,350,128 has a contractual basis. Considering that Hong Xiufeng has failed to provide sufficient evidence for the nature of the RMB 7,360,000 she collected, this amount may be correspondingly deducted from the total liquidated damages to better balance the interests of the parties. Accordingly, Anbeijia Company shall pay Hong Xiufeng liquidated damages in the amount of RMB 11,990,128. Pursuant to Article 113(1) of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, if a party fails to perform its contractual obligations or performs them in a manner that does not conform to the agreement, thereby causing losses to the other party, the amount of damages for loss shall be equivalent to the losses caused by the breach. The expenditure of RMB 3,000,000 in attorney's fees is not necessarily incurred by Hong Xiufeng in asserting her rights. Since the parties have no specific agreement on this matter, and Hong Xiufeng has not sufficiently proven a direct causal relationship between this loss and Anbeijia Company's breach, this court does not support this claim by Hong Xiufeng.

In conclusion, the first instance judgment erroneously determined that the legal relationship between the parties was a private lending relationship in the name of a housing sale and dismissed Hong Xiufeng's claims based on that determination. This constitutes an error in fact-finding and application of law, and this court corrects it. Hong Xiufeng's appeal asserting the existence of a commercial housing sale legal relationship between her and Anbeijia Company, and seeking Anbeijia Company to bear liability for breach of contract, including continued performance, has factual and legal basis. This court supports the reasonable part of her claims. Pursuant to Article 170(1)(2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this court hereby renders judgment as follows:

1. The Civil Judgment (2014) Yun Gao Min Yi Chu Zi No. 9 of the Yunnan High People's Court is reversed;

2. Kunming Anbeijia Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, deliver to Hong Xiufeng the commercial spaces on the first and second floors of Baifuqi Commercial Plaza;

3. Kunming Anbeijia Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. shall, within forty days after the administrative violations related to Baifuqi Commercial Plaza are resolved, assist Hong Xiufeng in completing the registration of change of ownership for the commercial spaces on the first and second floors;

4. Kunming Anbeijia Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, pay Hong Xiufeng liquidated damages in the amount of RMB 11,990,128;

5. Hong Xiufeng's other claims are dismissed.

If Kunming Anbeijia Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. fails to perform its obligation to pay monetary amounts within the period specified in this judgment, it shall, in accordance with Article 253 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, double the interest on the debt for the period of delayed performance.

The first instance case acceptance fee of RMB 630,558.30 and the second instance case acceptance fee of RMB 630,558.30, totaling RMB 1,261,116.60, shall be borne by Kunming Anbeijia Real Estate Development Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
